member.name: T:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.BlackboardMismatchPolicy
member.summary: How restore treats payload entries that no longer line up with the live schema. Independent of direction: schema keys absent from the payload always keep their registered defaults (forward compatibility for schemas that added keys).

member.name: F:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.BlackboardMismatchPolicy.Strict
member.summary: Fail loudly: an unknown payload key, a changed value type, or a schema-name/scope mismatch throws.

member.name: F:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.BlackboardMismatchPolicy.Skip
member.summary:
Skip entries that don't fit the schema (schema evolution): the matching subset is restored over defaults, mismatched entries are dropped. Corrupt values still throw.
Data safety: a restore that would apply zero entries — mismatched header, every entry skipped, or an entry-less payload — leaves the target board completely untouched (live values preserved). Skip never resets a board to defaults without restoring at least one value; the documented "defaults + payload" post-state applies only once at least one payload entry matches the live schema.

member.name: T:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.IContainerCodec
member.summary: Non-generic marker for container codecs — mirrors . A container codec (payload version 6) serializes custom containers (including AsyncCompositeState subclasses) that the graph serializer has no built-in recipe for.

member.name: T:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.IContainerCodec`1
member.summary:
Division of labor with the graph serializer: the serializer owns child-graph recursion — it walks the container's onto the wire and rebuilds them on read; the codec owns the reconstruction recipe — its opaque payload rides in the node's ordinary logic slot (typically a key plus config, reusing the user's logic-codec keys for any non-graph children).
Order contract (normative): enumeration order = wire order = the children order passed to — order is identity, exactly as region order is for RegionMask bits. This leans on the hard requirement that enumeration is stable and deterministic (identical sequence every time); a container backed by an unordered collection corrupts reconstruction silently, and the graph serializer verifies the requirement in DEBUG builds with a second enumeration. The rebuilt container must surface the new instances via its own SubGraphs and keep IBlackboardSettable forwarding — those walks are what agent stamping and blackboard binding reach (the standing user-container contract). A container that hides graphs from SubGraphs serializes without them; such a container is already broken for stamping, and the serializer inherits that contract rather than validating it.
receives the unwrapped container (a sync-only container is unwrapped from its SyncLogicAdapter first); a codec rebuilding a sync-only container must wrap the result in the public SyncLogicAdapter itself so the node stays sync-runnable.
member.typeparam: The wire type — must match the logic codec's wire type, because the container payload rides in the same node DTO slot; the graph serializer rejects a mismatch at construction.

member.name: T:NxGraph.Serialization.Abstraction.IRegionSelectorRegistry
member.summary:
Maps dynamic-parallel region selectors to stable string keys so they can ride the graph payload (payload version 6): the write side turns the authored delegate into a key, the read side turns the key back into a delegate. Delegates themselves cannot ride a wire payload — the registry is the durable identity for them, analogous to how an keys node logic.
Both lookups follow the try-pattern so the serializer owns the error messages and can include node context. The trust model matches : the registry restores a delegate for the key — nothing verifies it behaves like the delegate the graph was authored with; that contract belongs to the user.
Delegate identity is reference identity: two lambdas with identical bodies are distinct delegates, so the graph must be authored with the registered instance for the write-side lookup to succeed.
